episodes.161574: Moderate southwest flow coupled with warm SST helped to promote morning showers and storms in the Gulf and along the coast. One of them storms produced a water spout off Pirates Harbor.
episodes.161693: Afternoon and evening showers over leeward parts of the Big Island of Hawaii became heavy after daytime heating and enhancement provided by a nearby upper level disturbance.  The rain caused small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways.  No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.162063: A line of thunderstorms developed during the afternoon of the 6th and persisted into the evening. The thunderstorms developed in advance of a cold front and upper level disturbance crossing the region. The strongest thunderstorms occurred across central and Downeast portions of the region. A severe thunderstorm produced damaging winds across portions of southern Penobscot county.
episodes.162065: A cold front moved south into Mississippi, with thunderstorms along the front producing heavy rain and some flash flooding.
episodes.163178: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved southwest across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and early evening hours. Thunderstorm winds produced considerable damage in Safford. Sporadic wind and lightning damage also occurred the greater Tucson Metro Area.
episodes.163222: A line of strong to severe thunderstorms resulted in damage across southern Herkimer County on Monday September 6, 2021.
episodes.163271: Isolated thunderstorms formed along a stationary front. Some of these storms produced damaging wind gusts.
episodes.163399: A cold front slow moved into the region sparking scattered thunderstorms. The very wet airmass in place allowed storms to produce high rain rates while slowly moving which produced flooding.
episodes.163452: A strong mid-level trough and weak surface cold front crossed the eastern Great Lakes Monday morning. A line of thunderstorms over southern Ontario moved across Lake Erie and eventually reached the western end of Lake Ontario around daybreak. It then moved down the length of Lake Ontario and into the eastern Lake Ontario region. Surface based instability was mainly confined close to the lake shores, which was an influence of the warm lake waters warming the boundary layer. This resulted in a few strong wind gusts along the shores of Lake Erie and Lake Ontario as the line passed.

episodes.163520: A sharp cold front moved through Maine on the afternoon of September 6th.  Strong dynamics aloft with this early fall trough brought amble amounts of shear to the region. In addition, enough low level instability developed due to very steep lapse rates that allowed for a few storms to became severe with damaging wind gusts across the Mid-coast of Maine and the Kennebec River Valley.
